title: Riemannian optimization on stiefel and grassmann manifolds

items.title: Real Stiefel and Grassmann optimization conventions
items.statement: Fix the real Stiefel space St(n,r)={X in R^(n by r): X^T X=I_r}, the quotient Grassmannian Gr(r,n)=St(n,r)/O(r), and the Frobenius inner products used on their tangent and horizontal representatives.

items.title: Complex Stiefel and Grassmann optimization conventions
items.statement: Define the complex Stiefel manifold St_C(n,r), its unitary quotient Gr_C(r,n), and the real Frobenius metric Re tr(U*V) on complex tangent spaces and horizontal representatives.

items.title: Finite-dimensional Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds are compact
items.statement: For 1<=r<=n, St(n,r) is a nonempty closed bounded subset of R^(n by r), and Gr(r,n) is its continuous quotient image; hence both are compact.

items.title: Finite-dimensional complex Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds are compact
items.statement: For 1<=r<=n, St_C(n,r) is a nonempty closed bounded subset of R^(2nr), and Gr_C(r,n) is its continuous quotient image; hence both are compact.

items.title: Tangent spaces and Frobenius projections on Stiefel and Grassmann
items.statement: For X in St(n,r), identify T_X St(n,r) with {Z:X^T Z+Z^T X=0} and its Frobenius projection with G-X sym(X^T G); identify T_[X]Gr(r,n) with horizontal representatives X^T Z=0 and project G horizontally as (I-XX^T)G.

items.title: Complex Stiefel and Grassmann tangent projections
items.statement: For complex orthonormal X, T_X St_C={Z:X*Z+Z*X=0} and the real-Frobenius Stiefel projection is G-X Herm(X*G); complex Grassmann tangent representatives are horizontal X*Z=0 with projection (I-XX*)G.

items.title: Projected Euclidean gradients are the Stiefel and Grassmann gradients
items.statement: For a smooth ambient objective, the induced Frobenius Riemannian gradient on St(n,r) is G-X sym(X^T G); if the objective is invariant under X to XQ for Q in O(r), the descended Grassmann gradient is (I-XX^T)G, and its zeros are precisely critical points.

items.title: Polar retraction on the complex Grassmannian
items.statement: For horizontal eta at [X] in complex Grassmann, define R_[X](eta) as the column space of (X+eta)((X+eta)*(X+eta))^(-1/2); the horizontal condition makes this defined for every eta and unitary-equivariant.

items.title: The complex Grassmann polar map is a first-order retraction
items.statement: The complex polar map is smooth on the horizontal tangent bundle, fixes zero, has identity differential there, and is independent of the orthonormal frame representative.

items.title: Gradient of a unitary-invariant Hermitian projector energy
items.statement: If E is a real C1 function of Hermitian matrices with Hermitian Frobenius gradient K(P), then E(XX*) descends to complex Grassmann and has horizontal gradient 2(I-XX*)K(XX*)X.

items.title: QR and polar retractions on Stiefel and Grassmann
items.statement: For tangent eta with X+eta full column rank, define the Stiefel QR retraction as the positive-diagonal reduced-QR Q factor and the polar retraction as (X+eta)((X+eta)^T(X+eta))^(-1/2); descend each to Grassmann by taking the column space.

items.title: The QR and polar maps are first-order Stiefel and Grassmann retractions
items.statement: On their full-rank domains, the positive-diagonal QR and polar maps are smooth, map into St(n,r), fix eta=0, and have differential the identity there; both induced Grassmann maps are representative-independent and first-order.

items.title: Finite-budget retraction Armijo backtracking
items.statement: For a nonstationary Stiefel or invariant Grassmann objective, test t=1,beta,beta^2,... up to a finite cap, reject rank-invalid trial points, and return the first retracted point satisfying the Armijo sufficient-decrease inequality or an explicit failure status.

items.title: Finite-budget Riemannian trust-region method
items.statement: Form the pullback quadratic model, use a Cauchy-decrease step or a finite-budget candidate satisfying the Cauchy fraction, apply the small-radius safeguard, and update the retracted actual-to-predicted ratio with the OPT3 eta and gamma branches.

items.title: Projected vector transport on Stiefel and Grassmann
items.statement: For a Stiefel tangent step eta use either QR or polar endpoint Y and transport Z by Z-Y sym(Y^T Z). For a Grassmann tangent use its unique horizontal representative eta and the polar endpoint Y; transport horizontal Z by (I-YY^T)Z.

items.title: Retraction trust-region ratios are accurate at small radii
items.statement: For a positive radius Delta>0, a first-order retraction with Lipschitz pullback gradient, bounded self-adjoint model, and Cauchy-fraction trial has positive predicted decrease and ratio at least eta_2 below the stated gradient-proportional threshold, with zero-operator conventions.

items.title: Projected vector transports return tangent representatives
items.statement: The two projected transport formulas are linear maps into the tangent space at the retracted point and the Grassmann formula is invariant under orthogonal changes of representative.

items.title: Uniform pullback smoothness guarantees an Armijo step
items.statement: If pullback gradients are uniformly L_R-Lipschitz on unit tangent balls and the Riemannian gradient is uniformly bounded by G, the rank-guarded finite backtracking accepts a step whenever its cap reaches delta=min(1,1/(2G),2(1-a)/L_R), with accepted t at least beta delta. The unit tangent-ball estimate is asserted for trial sizes 0<t<=delta; an earlier accepted trial may be larger.

items.title: Retraction Armijo reaches an epsilon-gradient iterate in finite budget
items.statement: If f is bounded below and every Armijo call reaches the uniform accepted-step bound, then among N accepted updates the best gradient norm squared is at most (f(X_0)-f_inf)/(a beta delta N), giving O(epsilon^(-2)) accepted steps to gradient norm epsilon.

items.title: Riemannian trust regions reach an epsilon-gradient iterate
items.statement: Under uniform pullback-gradient Lipschitzness, bounded model operators, the Cauchy-fraction and small-radius safeguards, and bounded objective below, the finite-budget Riemannian trust-region method reaches gradient norm epsilon in O(epsilon^(-2)) accepted and rejected outer trials.

title: Riemannian optimization on stiefel and grassmann manifolds — Examples

items.title: A repeated eigenvalue gives a continuum of Grassmann minimizers
items.statement: For A=diag(0,0,2), the rank-one trace objective on Gr(1,3) has every line in span(e_1,e_2) as a global minimizer.

items.title: A strict saddle of a quadratic Stiefel objective
items.statement: For A=diag(0,1,2), the objective x^T A x on St(3,1) has a critical point at e_2 with a descending tangent curve and an ascending tangent curve.

items.title: A trace eigenspace objective and a Lanczos start-angle bound
items.statement: For A=diag(5,2,0), minimize -tr(X^T A X) on St(3,1); compute a two-dimensional Krylov candidate and check its objective gap and the source theorem's start-angle bound.
